fact_text: The owner says his first restaurant venture, a partnership started in 2001, made losses and was closed after about 10 to 11 months, costing his family's investment.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: After that failure a friend lent the money within three days, and the owner and his brothers restarted with no days off and no trips home.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: Café Imran began as a simple dhaba-style menu of daal, chana and vegetables, with mutton rare and beef the usual meat.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner set a target of filling the breakfast tables with vehicle-based customers between 6 and 7 am, and said breakfast became the restaurant's strongest meal.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The restaurant had no dessert because its customers, mainly drivers, did not order one; the owner used good tea as the dessert, reasoning that it makes guests overlook minor food flaws.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said lunch later became his best meal, while dinner depends on the kadhai, which the restaurant struggled to make well until a cook joined.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: In 2009 the owner bought five or six cheap, aged goats to save money, and the resulting kadhai was so tough that a customer returned it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said the cheap goats he bought were 10 to 11 kg animals, not large goats, and that they were unsuitable for kadhai.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: A cook named Ibrahim joined the restaurant and gradually built the dinner rhythm around the kadhai, which the owner says is the signature of evening dining.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: In 2009 the owner added fast food after a wider trend, sending a vehicle to Karachi to buy about 60,000 rupees of goods and hiring a cook for the menu.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: A Karachi business associate advised the owner to stay with his core dal and kadhai menu, and he later ended the fast-food line, running off the stock before stopping.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said the menu and taste must keep improving, because loyal guests get bored and stop coming if the food stays the same.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner first kept the barbecue section inside the restaurant rather than at the front, because staff did not know barbecue and many guests could not afford it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said the sales staff often said no to customers, so he hung pictures of barbecue dishes on the walls to attract guests who were not being offered them.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: Roshan, a dish the owner described as a Kota specialty, is supplied through a supply chain, and the owner said meals without it taste flat.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner prefers young dumba (fat-tailed sheep) of about 18 kg; he said it costs more per kg but gives much better taste.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: Café Imran uses its own kadhai masala recipe, buying whole spices and grinding and powdering them in-house on its own machines.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The new restaurant sits on about 3 acres outside Karachi in Gharo, styled as a farmhouse with greenery, indoor air-conditioned seating and outdoor takht seating.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: Indoor air-conditioned seating is 250 seats, and an extra 150-person corporate hall brings indoor seating to about 400.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: Outdoor seating is about 700, so combined seating is about 1,100, and with extra overflow space the owner put total seating at around 1,200 to 1,250.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The 150-person corporate hall is used for events on Saturdays and Sundays and counts toward indoor capacity.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said the 2030 vision includes branch expansion, and that seating was too small, so the team planned to extend seating in later years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said tourists visiting the historic Makli necropolis near Thatta, including visitors from China, Germany and Japan, are a customer opportunity for the restaurant.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said hygiene is a core strategy: the restaurant follows food authority rules and international SOPs, because cleanliness brings customers by word of mouth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said Dubai has a law giving diners the right to watch their food being cooked, and he adopted open-kitchen service in Pakistan without a legal requirement.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said open-kitchen cooking keeps cooks alert and energetic, because they know the guest is watching them.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: On 5 Dec 2025 the owner said the restaurant had run for about 10 months at its new site, with strong customer feedback, and called running a fine-dining restaurant a major challenge.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner said a restaurant that stops trading turns every cost into a loss, including food stock, staff pay and electricity.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: The owner advised aspiring restaurateurs to learn SOPs and work in an established business before investing, because a failed setup with no experience costs a lot of money.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)

fact_text: Early on the restaurant ran with only the owner, his brothers, a dishwasher and two tandoor staff, with the owner dividing the work across his brothers to save costs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Roadside Dhaba to Fine Dining: The Inspiring Story of Café Imran | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-05)
